one_line: A shared drawing canvas whose WebMCP tools refuse stale or conflicting agent batches when a human intervenes.
what_it_does: Lets an agent draw, detects human changes through revisions, drops stale batches, forces reinspection and replanning, and protects human marks.
leverage_rationale: The page’s refusal, revision, and replanning protocol directly addresses shared human-agent state and pull-only WebMCP limitations; generic UI driving cannot provide comparable guarantees.
leverage_evidence: Transcript documents a human drawing seven strokes mid-batch, blocked canvas_batch, reinspection, replanning, and final axle integration.
About text specifies nine tools, revision locking, batch dropping, and human-mark protection.
Frame sheets show evolving canvas, colored status badges, and BARGE IN/tool-log sections.
execution_rationale: The 170-second video and transcript provide unusually direct end-to-end evidence of interruption, refusal, observation, replanning, and visible result; the drawing is intentionally crude but coherent for scope.
execution_evidence: Submitted video with detailed transcript and alive demo.
Frame sheets show iterative canvas states and structured log panels.
Transcript gives timestamps and concrete blocked/replanned actions.
impact_rationale: Human control over agent edits in shared documents is a real safety and collaboration problem, and the protocol generalizes beyond drawing.
impact_evidence: Project explicitly connects the canvas problem to shared documents and agent edits.
Demonstrated protection of human marks and explicit plan changes.
creativity_rationale: The project turns WebMCP’s pull-only limitation into the core interaction model, inventing a memorable refusal-and-replan protocol rather than hiding the limitation.
creativity_evidence: ‘The page can say no’ is pursued through stale-call refusal, forced observation, and declared replanning.
Transcript shows the agent integrates human wheels rather than merely leaving them untouched.
usability_note: The explicit refusal and replan states make shared control legible; the intentionally crude drawing is not a usability defect for this reference implementation.
red_flags: Drawing quality is intentionally rough, so visual polish should not be over-weighted.
Generalization beyond the demonstrated canvas is argued rather than tested.
standouts: Exceptional direct evidence of WebMCP conflict handling.
Novel pull-only protocol with clear safety semantics.
advance_reason: Outstanding leverage and creativity with direct, transcript-backed execution evidence.
